title: Work Health and Safety Act 2020
abstract: The Work Health and Safety Act 2020 establishes Western Australia's primary legislative framework for workplace health and safety. The Act defines key stakeholders including persons conducting businesses or undertakings (PCBUs), officers, workers, and other persons at workplaces, each with specific duties and obligations. It outlines primary duty of care requirements, incident notification obligations, and consultation requirements. The legislation introduces industrial manslaughter provisions and establishes a tiered penalty structure for non-compliance ranging from Category 1 to Category 3 offences. This Act provides the foundational legal requirements for all workplace health and safety practices in Western Australia, including traffic management operations.

complianceNotes.note: Industrial Manslaughter (Section 30A): A PCBU or officer commits a crime if their conduct causes death and they knew the conduct was likely to cause death or serious harm, acting in disregard of that likelihood. Maximum penalty: 20 years imprisonment and $5 million fine for individuals; $10 million for body corporates.
complianceNotes.consequence: Criminal prosecution with imprisonment and substantial fines

complianceNotes.note: Category 1 Offence (Section 31): Failure to comply with health and safety duty involving reckless conduct exposing an individual to risk of death or serious injury. Maximum penalty: $3.5 million for body corporate, $700,000 or 5 years imprisonment for individual PCBU, $350,000 or 5 years imprisonment for officer.
complianceNotes.consequence: Criminal prosecution with imprisonment and substantial fines

complianceNotes.note: Primary Duty of Care (Section 19): PCBUs must ensure, so far as reasonably practicable, the health and safety of workers and others. This includes providing safe work environment, safe plant and structures, safe systems of work, and adequate facilities for workers.
complianceNotes.consequence: Foundation for all WHS compliance obligations

complianceNotes.note: Officer Due Diligence (Section 27): Officers must exercise due diligence to ensure the PCBU complies with its duties. This includes acquiring and keeping up-to-date knowledge of WHS matters, gaining an understanding of hazards and risks, and ensuring appropriate resources and processes are available.
complianceNotes.consequence: Personal liability for officers including directors and senior executives

complianceNotes.note: Incident Notification (Section 38): PCBUs must notify the regulator immediately after becoming aware of a notifiable incident (death, serious injury/illness, or dangerous incident). The incident site must be preserved until an inspector arrives or directs otherwise (Section 39).
complianceNotes.consequence: Failure to notify can result in significant penalties; site disturbance may constitute an offence

complianceNotes.note: Consultation Requirements (Section 47): PCBUs must consult with workers who carry out work for the business and who are (or are likely to be) directly affected by a health and safety matter. Consultation must be meaningful and allow workers to contribute to decision-making.
complianceNotes.consequence: Failure to consult may result in penalties and undermines WHS culture

complianceNotes.note: Worker Duties (Section 28): Workers must take reasonable care for their own health and safety, take reasonable care that their acts or omissions do not adversely affect others, and comply with reasonable instructions and policies.
complianceNotes.consequence: Workers can be prosecuted for breaches of their duties

complianceNotes.note: Right to Cease Unsafe Work (Section 84): Workers have the right to cease or refuse to carry out work if they have a reasonable concern that carrying out the work would expose them to a serious risk to their health and safety.
complianceNotes.consequence: PCBUs must not disadvantage workers for exercising this right

complianceNotes.note: Improvement and Prohibition Notices (Part 10): Inspectors can issue improvement notices requiring compliance or prohibition notices stopping dangerous work. Failure to comply with notices is an offence with substantial penalties.
complianceNotes.consequence: Non-compliance with notices results in additional offences and penalties

complianceNotes.note: Health and Safety Representatives (Part 5 Division 3): Workers can request election of HSRs who have powers including inspecting workplaces, accompanying inspectors, investigating complaints, and issuing provisional improvement notices.
complianceNotes.consequence: PCBUs must facilitate HSR functions and cannot discriminate against HSRs
